paper_metadata.title: Quantum-Assisted AI for Speeding up Large-Scale Data Processing

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum‑classical Quantum‑Assisted AI (QAAI) framework using QSVM, QNN, and variational quantum circuits with amplitude/basis encoding and randomized measurement protocols. It reports empirical improvements such as 30–40% faster training, 92.5% healthcare classification accuracy versus 85% for classical SVM, and 93% cybersecurity anomaly‑detection precision versus 82% classical, but provides no dataset sizes, qubit counts, or reproducible benchmarking details.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical QAAI framework for large-scale data processing, evaluated on healthcare, finance, and cybersecurity datasets using QSVM, QNN, variational quantum circuits, and randomized measurement protocols on IBM Quantum/PennyLane.

algorithm.variant: hybrid quantum-classical QAAI framework with QSVM, QNN, and VQC components

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical data encoded into quantum states using amplitude encoding for financial data and basis encoding for healthcare patient records; quantum kernel estimation used for QSVM and variational gates used for learning parameters.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Improve classification, prediction, and anomaly detection performance for large-scale data processing while reducing training time and improving noise resilience.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: randomized measurement protocol for noise resilience; hybrid quantum-classical optimization for parameter tuning

problem_instance.description: Three application scenarios: healthcare diagnostic classification, financial market trend prediction, and cybersecurity anomaly detection.

dataset_specification.description: Healthcare patient diagnostic records; stock market trend and real-time trading patterns; network traffic data. No specific ticker symbols, date range, or split reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalization, feature scaling, and data balancing; amplitude encoding for financial data; basis encoding for healthcare data; randomized measurement protocol for cybersecurity data.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Multiple iterations; metrics reported include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. No explicit cross-validation or number of runs reported.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise / gate errors / input-data noise

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Normalization, feature scaling, and data balancing.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: conventional AI model / traditional AI counterpart
speedup_claims.conditions: large-scale, high-dimensional datasets; hybrid QAAI framework
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as a training-speed reduction; no raw timing values, dataset sizes, or number of runs provided.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; paper does not report qubit counts, circuit depth, dataset size, or runtime measurements required to estimate crossover.
